tools.name: search_listings
tools.description: Search published AI agents, MCP servers and skills in the directory by name, tagline or description.

tools.name: get_listing
tools.description: Fetch one published listing by its slug, with full description and links.

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: List the category ids a submission can be filed under. Call this before submit_listing. That tool takes category ids, not names.

tools.name: trending
tools.description: Listings gaining momentum right now, ranked by heat (the 0-100 engagement score), upvotes or new reviews over a rolling window. Paid listings get no ranking preference here; the `featured` flag says which ones are paid.

tools.name: discover
tools.description: Browse the directory by vertical, category, pricing and access model. Use this when the ask is a kind of product rather than a name, e.g. 'open-source MCP servers for databases', 'free coding agents'.

tools.name: find_alternatives
tools.description: Alternatives and competitors to a product. Takes a listing slug, a website URL, or just the product name, including products that are not in the directory, in which case the closest listings by topic come back instead.

tools.name: compare
tools.description: Compare 2-5 listings side by side on pricing, access model, categories, heat, upvotes and rating. Takes slugs. Resolve them with search_listings or find_alternatives first.

tools.name: new_launches
tools.description: The most recently published listings in the directory.

tools.name: submit_listing
tools.description: Submit a product to the directory on behalf of the connected user. The listing enters the same pending review queue as a web submission; the returned URL is where the submitter finishes and tracks it. tools.name: submit_review
tools.description: Leave a review on a listing on behalf of the connected user: a 1-5 star rating and an optional note on what worked and what did not. findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: trending, submit_listing, submit_review · Public sink: submit_listing, submit_review.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: trending, submit_listing, submit_review · Public sink: submit_listing, submit_review

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
